tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user wants to assess, audit, or review...'), focuses on user intent (security posture of Bedrock workloads), explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name a specific control, and is concise (a short paragraph).
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to assess, audit, or review the security posture of Amazon Bedrock generative-AI workloads in an AWS account, across regions or associated accounts. Apply it even when the user does not name a specific control, for example when they ask whether their Bedrock guardrails, knowledge bases, agents, or custom models are set up securely..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what KMS or IAM is) and jumps straight into domain-specific scope, safety rules, and workflow steps specific to this skill. It is dense but each section conveys non-obvious, skill-specific information.
tests.evidence: Covers guardrail coverage, KMS encryption, VPC endpoints, agent and action-group IAM least privilege...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables, API docs, or error-code lists are embedded in the body; detailed check logic is deferred to references/bedrock-checks.md and referenced conditionally rather than inlined.
tests.evidence: Open [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check. Each entry gives the read-only API call(s), the pass/fail/N-A logic, severity, verifiability, resolution text...

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both reference files are linked via markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific step/condition explaining when to load it (e.g., region resolution, running checks, report assembly).
tests.evidence: See [references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md) → "Region resolution". ... Open [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Safety-critical and fragile sections (read-only safety, verify-vs-prescribe rules) are given exact, prescriptive instructions, while flexible sections (e.g., general workflow framing, coordinating with other skills) leave room for agent judgment appropriately.
tests.evidence: NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes, attaches, enables, disables, or otherwise mutates a resource... Never call a non-Get/List/Describe verb

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same job as equal options; it specifies the correct SDK client (bedrock-agent) vs IAM prefix (bedrock:) deterministically rather than offering alternatives.
tests.evidence: Bedrock prompts, agents, knowledge bases, flows, and agent action groups are called through the bedrock-agent SDK client... but their IAM actions use the bedrock: prefix

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (resolve scope/regions, run checks, validate, report) applicable to any Bedrock assessment request, not a one-off declaration for a specific account/resource.
tests.evidence:
Step 1: Confirm intent and scope (read-only, accounts in scope)
- [ ] Step 2: Resolve target regions
- [ ] Step 3: Run every Bedrock check per region

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes explicit gotcha-like corrections such as the bedrock-agent vs bedrock: prefix confusion and the AWS-owned-key encryption nuance, which are concrete non-obvious corrections for this domain.
tests.evidence: A missing modelKmsKeyArn or serverSideEncryptionConfiguration is reported as "AWS-owned key", never as "unencrypted".
